question: In a star network, how many lines are required for connecting N nodes to the host node?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In star topology, 'n-1' lines are required for connecting 'n' nodes.**
 
• **Star topology** is a network topology in which all nodes **(computers, servers, peripherals, and other devices)** are connected to a **central hub or switch.**
 
• The **central hub **acts as a mediator to transmit data between nodes and manages the communication between them.
 
• 
 
In a **star topology**, each node has a dedicated point-to-point connection to the central hub, which eliminates the need for nodes to pass data through other nodes to reach the intended destination.

 
 
• 
 
The central hub serves as a communication channel for the **connected nodes**, and it is responsible for directing data traffic from one node to another.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the context of computer networking, topology refers to the physical or logical arrangement of nodes (devices such as computers, servers, and other network devices) and the connections between them in a network.There are several types of network topologies, including:
 
 
• **Bus topology:** In this topology, all devices are connected to a single communication line, called a bus. Data is transmitted from one device to another over the bus.
 
• **Star topology:** In this topology, all devices are connected to a central hub or switch. Data is transmitted from one device to another via the hub.
 
• **Ring topology:** In this topology, all devices are connected in a closed loop. Data is transmitted in one direction around the loop, from one device to another.
 
• **Mesh topology:** In this topology, every device is connected to every other device in the network. This creates multiple paths for data to travel, which can increase network redundancy and resilience.
 
• **Tree topology: **In this topology, devices are arranged in a hierarchical structure, resembling a tree. Devices are connected to parent nodes, which are connected to other parent nodes, and so on, until the root node is reached.
 
• The choice of topology depends on the specific needs and requirements of the network, including factors such as cost, scalability, fault tolerance, and performance.
